'''Stephanie A. Burns''' (born January 24, 1955) is an American [[organosilicon]] chemist and businesswoman, who served as president and CEO of [[Dow Corning]] from 2003 to 2011. She has also served as honorary president of [[Society of Chemical Industry]].

==Early life and education==

Burns, the daughter of an English and history professor father who was the dean of continuing education at Florida International University in Miami, and a real estate agent mother, was born in [[Torrington, Wyoming]]. As a child, Burns was fascinated by the world around her.<ref name=":1" /> Burns's father constantly found her trying to dissect frogs and snakes.<ref name=":1" /> He supposedly instilled in her the importance of education and challenging herself.<ref name=":1" /> In Junior High Burns gained interest in her science and math classes leading her to declare her major in chemistry on her very first day of college.<ref name=":1" />

While attending Florida International University Burns's organic chemistry professor, Arthur Herriott, first excited her about organosilicon chemistry.<ref name=":1" /> Burns graduated with a bachelor's degree from [[Florida International University]] in Miami in 1977. For graduate work, Herriott directed Burns to Thomas J. Barton, a specialist in organosilicon chemistry at Iowa State University, where Burns would earn her Ph.D. in organic chemistry in 1982.<ref name=":1" /> During Burns time at Iowa State is when she was acquainted with Dow Corning, who had funded some of her research.<ref name=":1" /> After graduating from [[Iowa State University]],<ref name="chemheritage.org" /> Burns conducted her postdoctoral studies at [[University of Montpellier]] in France.<ref name="GSK">{{cite web|url=http://www.gsk.com/en-gb/about-us/board-of-directors/dr-stephanie-burns/|title=Dr Stephanie Burns|publisher=GSK|access-date=16 November 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117023057/http://www.gsk.com/en-gb/about-us/board-of-directors/dr-stephanie-burns/|archive-date=17 November 2015}}</ref> which she then followed up by joining Dow Corning to continue her research.<ref name=":1" />

==Career==

Burns joined [[Dow Corning]] in 1982<ref name=Zipkin2007>{{cite news|last1=Zipkin|first1=Amy|title=Delight in Science, Then and Now|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/01/28/business/yourmoney/28boss.html?_r=0|accessdate=15 November 2015|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=28 January 2007}}</ref> in France as a researcher and specialist in [[organosilicon]] chemistry, which is the study into compounds made of [[carbon]] and [[silicon]].<ref name=chemheritage.org/> Burns's research in silicones, and new heat-resistant rubber creation has earned her three patents that she was credited in her first years at the company.<ref name="chemheritage.org" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=From Lab Bench To Executive Suite|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/89/i18/Lab-Bench-Executive-Suite.html|access-date=2020-11-17|website=Chemical & Engineering News|language=en}}</ref> She gradually worked her way into corporate management at [[Dow Corning]], and in 1994 she was appointed director of Women's Health and was part of the Chapter 11 management team.<ref>{{cite book|title=Dun & Bradstreet Reference Book of Corporate Managements|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=x61ZAAAAYAAJ|year=2008|publisher=Dun & Bradstreet, Incorporated|page=448}}</ref> In 1997, she moved to [[Brussels]], after being appointed Science and Technology Director for Europe.<ref name="GSK"/>

Upon her return to the United States in 2000, Burns was appointed executive vice president of the firm, and three years later became its president, the first woman to do so.<ref name=chemheritage.org>{{cite web|url=http://www.chemheritage.org/discover/online-resources/chemistry-in-history/themes/petrochemistry-and-synthetic-polymers/synthetic-polymers/burns.aspx|title=Stephanie Burns|publisher=Chemical Heritage Foundation|access-date=15 November 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160712164316/http://www.chemheritage.org/discover/online-resources/chemistry-in-history/themes/petrochemistry-and-synthetic-polymers/synthetic-polymers/burns.aspx|archive-date=July 12, 2016}}</ref> She served as the president and chief executive officer of [[Dow Corning]], from February 2003 until her retirement on 31 December 2011.<ref name="GSK"/> She also served as its chief operating officer from January 2004, and as chairman from January 2006, until her retirement,<ref name="GSK"/> replacing Gary E. Anderson.<ref>{{cite book|title=Chemical Week|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EfRJAQAAIAAJ|year=2005|publisher=McGraw-Hill|page=168}}</ref> Under Burns's leadership, [[Dow Corning]] expanded their range to include more than 7,000 silicon-based products.<ref name=":0" /> Additionally, she has overseen extensive diversification of the company's reach extending into new geographic markets.<ref name=":0" /> In Burns tenure at the top of [[Dow Corning]], she has led them to nearly quintuple their profits, and raised their annual spending on R&D to 6% of their total sails.<ref name=":1" /> In 2011 Burns received the [[International Palladium Medal|International Palladium medal]] from the [[Société de Chimie Industrielle (American Section)|Société de Chimie Industrielle]] for her many distinguished contributions to the chemical industry and, contributing to the enhancement of the international aims and objectives of the [[Société de Chimie Industrielle (American Section)|Société de Chimie Industrielle]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2010-10-12|title=Dr. Stephanie A. Burns, Chairman, President, and Chief Executive Officer of Dow Corning, to be Awarded the 2011 International Palladium Medal|url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20101012005257/en/Dr.-Stephanie-A.-Burns-Chairman-President-and-Chief-Executive-Officer-of-Dow-Corning-to-be-Awarded-the-2011-International-Palladium-Medal|access-date=2020-11-16|website=www.businesswire.com|language=en}}</ref> Burns is the first woman to receive this award, which was presented to her at a dinner in her honor on May 3, 2011, in the Grand Ballroom of the Roosevelt Hotel in New York.<ref name=":0" />

==Service on councils and boards==

Burns has also served as honorary president of the [[Society of Chemical Industry]],<ref name=soci.org2012>{{cite web|title=Dr Stephanie Burns joins Corning Board of Directors|url=http://www.soci.org/News/Press/press-Burns-Corning|publisher=Society of Chemical Industry|accessdate=15 November 2015|date=2 February 2012}}</ref> as chairwoman of the [[American Chemistry Council]], and on the boards of the [[Michigan Molecular Institute]] and the [[Society for Women's Health Research]].<ref name="GSK"/> Burns also was appointed by [[Barack Obama|President Barack Obama]] to the [[President's Export Council]].<ref name=":0" />
